buyersGuidePage.heading: Buyer’s Guide
buyersGuidePage.intro: From the buying process and financing to taxes and frequently asked questions — everything international buyers need to know about purchasing property in London, in one place.

whyInvest: A global destination for living, education and business
internationalBuyersGuide.ctaHeading: Considering Purchasing Property in the UK?

taxesAndFees.q: What Taxes Apply When Buying Property?
taxesAndFees.a1: When purchasing a property, buyers are generally subject to purchase-related taxes such as Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT). The amount payable depends on the structure of the purchase and your individual circumstances, and is detailed for you by your solicitor during the transaction.
taxesAndFees.a2: Once you own the property, any ongoing tax obligations and annual filings can be handled with guidance from professional accountants and tax advisors.

options.title: Cash Buyers
options.body: Purchasing the property outright with equity. As there is no mortgage process involved, the purchase generally moves faster.

options.title: UK Mortgages
options.body: Buyers who reside or earn income in the UK can access a range of mortgage products. Eligibility is assessed based on income, credit history, and overall financial profile.

options.title: International Mortgages
options.body: Some banks and specialist lenders offer mortgages to buyers living abroad. Lending terms vary depending on country of residence and individual financial circumstances.

options.title: Payment Plans
options.body: On new-build developments, payment plans offered by developers allow the purchase price to be paid in stages throughout construction. Payment plans vary by project.

financingOptions.ctaHeading: Which Financing Option Is Right For You?
financingOptions.ctaBody: Whether you are purchasing with cash or exploring mortgage options, our team can help you understand the available routes and identify suitable opportunities.

items.q: Who Can Buy Property in the UK?
items.a: To purchase property in the UK, you do not need to be a British citizen or resident. International investors, foreign nationals, and individuals living abroad can all buy residential property in the UK.

items.q: Required Documents
items.a: Certain documents are requested throughout the purchasing process for identity verification and legal requirements. These typically include a passport, proof of address, and documentation showing the source of funds. Requirements may vary depending on the nature of the purchase.

items.q: Identity Verification & AML Checks
items.a: All buyers in the UK go through identity and source-of-funds verification as part of anti-money laundering (AML) regulations. These checks are a standard and legal part of every purchase.

items.q: Transferring Funds to the UK
items.a: For international buyers, purchase payments are made through secure banking channels — usually via SWIFT transfer — once your solicitor has completed the required legal checks and verification process.

items.q: Can I Obtain a Mortgage?
items.a: Yes. Both UK residents and international investors can access mortgage options. Eligibility is assessed based on income, credit history, and overall financial profile.

items.q: Can I Rent Out My Property?
items.a: Yes. Many investors generate rental income by letting out their property. There is strong tenant demand across many areas of London and the wider UK, with potential rental yields varying by location, property features, and market conditions. Upon request, MAK Global guides you step by step through the letting process — from finding a suitable tenant to property management — providing the necessary information throughout. However, mortgage terms, tenancy regulations, and building management rules should be taken into account.

items.q: How Long Does the Purchase Process Take?
items.a: The process can vary depending on the type of property being purchased. Completed properties can typically be purchased within a few weeks, while for new-build developments the completion date depends on the developer’s delivery schedule.

items.q: Do I Need a Solicitor to Purchase Property in the UK?
items.a: Yes. Purchasing property in the UK requires working with a solicitor or licensed conveyancer. Your solicitor handles critical stages on your behalf, including reviewing contracts, conducting title checks, carrying out legal due diligence, transferring funds, and completing the purchase.

items.q: Do I Need to Visit the UK to Buy Property?
items.a: No. You can purchase property without travelling to the UK. Reservation, legal processes, and identity verification can all be completed remotely through secure digital channels with your solicitor’s support.

items.q: What Is the Difference Between Freehold and Leasehold?
items.a: Freehold is a form of ownership where you own the property and the land it stands on outright, with no time limit. Leasehold means you have the right to use the property for a fixed period, while ownership of the land remains with another party.

items.q: Do You Need to Open a UK Bank Account?
items.a: In most cases, opening a UK bank account is not required. Purchases can be completed through international bank transfers. However, in some situations, a local bank account may provide added convenience.

items.q: Is Support Available in Turkish?
items.a: You won’t face any issues. At MAK Global, we provide Turkish-language support at every stage of the purchasing process. Our team includes Turkish-speaking consultants, and where needed, we can connect you with solicitors, accountants, and mortgage specialists who offer service in Turkish. From reservation through to completion, we provide clear and transparent guidance at every stage — helping you manage the process confidently even without English.

items.q: What Are the Main Costs When Buying Property in England?
items.a: Main costs include legal fees and, where applicable, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT). Mortgage purchases may involve lending and valuation fees, while surveys, searches, and Land Registry charges can also apply. In England, the selling estate agent's commission is generally paid by the seller.

items.q: What Ongoing Costs May Arise After Owning a Property in England?
items.a: Ongoing costs depend on the property type and how it is used. Leasehold apartments may have service charges and, in some cases, ground rent. Letting management, insurance, maintenance, and repairs can also add costs. Council Tax is usually paid by the occupier, while rental profits must be declared under the relevant tax rules.

items.q: How Much Are Solicitor's Fees?
items.a: UK law requires that the transfer of title be handled by solicitors acting for both the buyer and the seller. Fees for this typically range from £1,500 to £4,000.

items.q: What Additional Costs Can Arise When Buying a Property?
items.a: In addition to the purchase price, costs may include solicitor or conveyancer fees, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT), surveys, and search fees. Mortgage purchases may also involve application and valuation charges. The total cost depends on the property's price, financing method, and the buyer's circumstances.

items.q: Can I Buy a Property to Let Out Using an Overseas Mortgage?
items.a:
A citizen of any country living and working outside the UK (Turkey, for example) can obtain a "Buy to Let" mortgage in the UK. You do not need to be a UK resident to do so. Depending on your rental income and prevailing interest rates, banks can lend up to 75% of the property's value.
This way, part of your rental income covers your mortgage payments while — depending on current interest/market rates — leaving you with some income on top. As a rule, banks look for your rental yield to be at least 1.2–1.4 times the mortgage interest (depending on market conditions), and set your minimum required deposit accordingly.

items.q: Why Is Location Important When Investing in UK Property?
items.a: Location should be selected according to your investment purpose. The criteria will differ depending on whether the property is for your own use, for your child, or to generate rental income. For personal use, budget and lifestyle are key, while investment purchases should focus on rental yield and return potential.

items.q: Is It Better to Purchase a Property Personally or Through a Company?
items.a: The most suitable purchasing structure may vary depending on your investment plan and objectives. MAK Global will connect you with its professional partners and mortgage specialists according to your investment strategy, helping you evaluate your options and make the most suitable decision.

items.q: How Does Someone With a UK Tax Liability Pay Their Tax?
items.a: UK tax obligations are handled through HMRC. Depending on the circumstances, registration with HMRC and an annual Self Assessment return may be required. The Non-Resident Landlord Scheme can also be relevant for overseas landlords. Tax treatment differs between personal ownership and ownership through a company.

items.q: Do I Need to Pay Tax on Rental Income in the UK?
items.a: Tax on rental income may vary depending on the individual's total income, tax position, and applicable tax regulations. Our experienced partners and qualified accountants will provide you with the necessary information from the beginning of your investment process.

items.q: Why Might a Newly Built Property Be Preferable for Investment?
items.a: A large part of the UK's housing stock consists of older properties. Older homes may have higher maintenance, repair, and energy costs. New builds are generally more energy-efficient and can be more attractive for rental or resale. Meeting EPC standards may also require additional upgrades in older properties.
